title: Object comparison extending a prescribed augmented cycle map
statement:
Let $A,B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and let $F:A\to B$ be additive and preserve finite limits and finite colimits. Let $K,L$ be cochain complexes indexed by $\mathbb Z$, let $u:F(K)\to L$ be a complex map, and let $I,J$ be bicomplexes with horizontal index $\mathbb Z$ and resolution index $\mathbb N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Put $S_K=\operatorname{single}_0(K)$ and $S_L=\operatorname{single}_0(L)$, and let $e_I:S_K\to I$, $e_J:S_L\to J$ be bicomplex augmentations. For every horizontal degree $r$, put $\rho_K^r=\operatorname{singleObjXSelf}:S_K^{r,0}\xrightarrow{\sim}K^r$, define $\rho_L^r$ similarly, and put $\varepsilon_I^r=(e_I^r)^0(\rho_K^r)^{-1}$, $\varepsilon_J^r=(e_J^r)^0(\rho_L^r)^{-1}$. Write $G$ for applying $F$ to resolution complexes, $B_I^p=\operatorname{Im}(d_I^{p-1,p})$, and $\iota_{Z,J}^p:Z^p(J)\to J^p$ for the cycle inclusion. Injectivity below means injectivity in $B$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Fix $p,q\in\mathbb Z$ with $q=p+1$. Suppose the augmentations on the object and cycle columns in degree $p$, and on the outgoing boundary column $\operatorname{Im}(d^{q-1,q})$, are quasi-isomorphisms for both $I$ and $J$. Suppose those three columns of $J$ are termwise injective. Given a complex map $y:G(Z^p(I))\to Z^p(J)$ satisfying
$\iota_{Z,J}^{p,0}y^0 F((\operatorname{cyclesMap}e_I,p)^0)=\varepsilon_J^p u^p F(\rho_K^p)F(\iota_{Z,S_K}^{p,0})$,
there is a complex map $x:G(I^p)\to J^p$ with $x^0F(\varepsilon_I^p)=\varepsilon_J^pu^p$ and $xG(\iota_{Z,I}^p)=\iota_{Z,J}^py$. No incoming boundary map or homology comparison is a hypothesis, and no outgoing boundary map is part of the conclusion.

proof.text: Construct the kernel/object/image row explicitly as cartanEilenbergCycleObjectRow. Its zero composite follows by cancellation of image.ι and iCycles_d. The private Lean helper cycleObjectRow_shortExact identifies iCycles as the kernel of factorThruImage via cyclesIsKernel and isKernelOfComp; factorThruImage is epi. ShortExact.map_of_exact maps the source row through F and evaluates both rows, producing exactly the degreewise exactness inputs for the horseshoe theorem.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-ce-comparison-augmented-rows] to identify the source and target rows with augmented short exact base rows S,T and a base-row map f induced by u. This gives the six augmentation quasi-isomorphisms and the four degree-zero transport equations. Bundle the three target columns as InjectiveResolution structures, using the given termwise injectivity proofs and these augmentations.

Lift f.τ₃ from the exact augmented source outgoing-image column to the bundled target outgoing-image injective resolution. The Lean construction is InjectiveResolution.descOfQuasiIso; descOfQuasiIso_commutes gives the strict augmented square. This is the nonnegative-resolution specialization of [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso].

Use from_single_hom_ext to reduce the prescribed cycle augmentation square to degree zero. Cancel the monomorphic degree-zero cycle inclusion of J, substitute the first transport equation, apply hy, and use the second transport equation. This proves the exact endpoint equation needed for the prescribed cycle map y.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift-exact-source] to S,T,f and the two augmented kernel/object/image rows. Prescribe the cycle endpoint y and the outgoing lift constructed above. The augmentation morphisms give both row squares, and the private exactness helper gives the degreewise exactness. Obtain x together with its augmentation square and its cycle inclusion square; discard only the unused outgoing square.

Evaluate the middle augmentation square in degree zero. Precompose by γ.hom and apply the third and fourth transport equations. This yields the original object augmentation equation. Retain it and the horseshoe cycle square as the two required conjuncts. The original theorem signature is unchanged.
